job.title: Field Service Engineer, WA
job.description:
Are you passionate about technology, problem-solving, and delivering exceptional service that makes a real impact in the Healthcare sector?

We’re looking for a Field Service Engineer to join a highly dedicated team and help ensure the reliability and performance of their cutting-edge clinical diagnostic equipment across Western Australia and other states.

About the organisation and the position

A leading manufacturer and distributor of IVD instruments and Research equipment is seeking an experienced Field Service Engineer to join their fast-growing team in Perth. As a key member of the Customer Care department, you’ll be the go-to technical expert supporting customers in laboratories and hospitals.

Your day-to-day will involve installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing and optimising biomedical instruments, while also ensuring that clients receive top-tier support that meets both industry and company standards.

This role is perfect for someone with a strong background in mechatronics, biomedical, or electrical engineering (or related disciplines), who’s comfortable working independently in the field and collaborating cross-functionally with internal teams.

Responsibilities

  • Provide technical service, repairs, and support to customers for diagnostic and research instruments (Haematology, Flow Cytometry, Coagulation, Urinalysis, Histology, etc.)

  • Troubleshoot hardware and software issues, escalating when needed to minimise downtime

  • Conduct pre-installation surveys, installations, and preventive maintenance

  • Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, and Technical Support to enhance customer satisfaction

  • Support project roll-outs

  • Attend conferences and training sessions

  • Manage company assets and resources responsibly

  • Be part of a rotating on-call roster - as required, depending on operational needs and customer support requirements

  • Travel to customers' sites across WA, including regional locations (interstate travel is expected from time to time, mainly for training, team collaboration, and business requirements)

Skills and experience

  • Tertiary qualification in Mechatronics, Biomedical, Electrical or Electronics Engineering (or related technical disciplines)

  • Experience supporting diagnostic, laboratory, medical device, or similar technical instrumentation environments 

  • Experience supporting laboratory automation and related IVD technologies - Haematology systems is preferred, while Histology/Digital Pathology experience will be highly regarded

  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical problem-solving skills

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a broad range of users

  • Experience working with Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), middleware solutions and Linux operating systems is advantageous

  • Highly organised, self-motivated and able to manage competing priorities independently 

  • Customer-focused with a proactive, collaborative approach

  • Current driver's licence and willingness to travel throughout Western Australia, including regional areas, as well as interstate when required.

What’s on offer

  • $95-110K Base + Super + Car Allowance + Bonus (commensurate with experience and skills)

  • A collaborative and supportive team environment

  • Ongoing training and professional development

  • A company that values quality, innovation, and continuous improvement.

  • Plenty of room to grow and take your career to the next level

 

We are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and empowered to succeed. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and identities, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, members of the LGBTQIA+ community and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from all qualified candidates.


For more details, please feel free to contact Chris – chris.danchald@tardis-group.com

job.title: Procurement & Contracting Manager
job.description:
Procurement & Contracting Manager

Major Capital Projects | Resources/Process Industry

Perth

 

Overview

A major global resources/process industry operator is seeking an experienced Procurement & Contracting Manager to support a significant capital projects portfolio across Australia and internationally.

 

This is a hands-on project procurement and contracting role, focused initially on running multiple large EPC/EPCM tender packages with international contractors. It requires someone who can operate across the full contracting lifecycle, from strategy and tendering through negotiation, award and contract management.

 

The role sits across procurement, contracting, commercial strategy and project execution support. It is not a narrow procurement role and not a pure post-award contracts administration position.

 

Key focus areas:

  • Contracting strategy and procurement planning
  • Market engagement and tender package preparation
  • Commercial/technical evaluation coordination
  • EPC/EPCM tendering and negotiation
  • Recommendation for award and contract formation
  • Post-award contract management
  • Claims, variations, commercial risk and contractor performance
  • Interface with project, engineering, legal, operations and contractor teams

 

The ideal background will include major capital project experience in one or more of:

  • Oil and gas/LNG
  • Mining/resources
  • Chemical processing
  • Major industrial infrastructure
  • Energy/process plant projects

 

Key requirements:

  • Senior procurement and contracting experience on major capital projects
  • EPC/EPCM contracting experience across strategy, tendering, negotiation and management
  • Ability to personally run large and complex tender packages
  • Strong commercial and contractual judgement
  • Experience dealing with international EPC/EPCM contractors
  • Exposure to claims, variations, disputes and contractor performance
  • Ability to work practically in a lean owner-side environment
  • Strong stakeholder interface across project, engineering, legal, commercial and operations teams

 

This role will suit someone who enjoys complex package strategy, major contractor engagement and hands-on commercial execution inside a major global operator with a substantial capital portfolio.

job.title: Construction Manager EOI
job.description:
Construction Manager / Site Senior Executive (SSE)

WA Gold Project | Owner's Team | Immediate Requirement

A WA gold producer is entering a critical phase of project execution and is seeking an experienced Construction Manager / SSE to provide site leadership during plant construction.

This is not a corporate project management role.

The focus is on safe execution, contractor performance, construction sequencing, statutory accountability and ensuring the project is delivered to plan in a live mining environment.

The Role

Reporting into the Project Director, you will take responsibility for site-based construction leadership across a significant mineral processing project.

You will work closely with contractors, owner's team personnel and operational stakeholders to ensure construction activities are safely executed, properly coordinated and aligned with project objectives.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide visible construction leadership across the site
• Manage contractor performance and site execution activities
• Maintain strong safety, quality and environmental standards
• Coordinate construction interfaces across multiple disciplines
• Drive schedule performance and construction readiness
• Support commissioning and transition planning activities
• Liaise with regulators, stakeholders and project leadership
• Fulfil Site Senior Executive responsibilities where required
• Ensure compliance with WA mining legislation and site management systems

About You

We are interested in speaking with proven construction leaders who have delivered major mining, mineral processing or heavy industrial projects.

You will ideally bring:

• Construction Manager, Site Manager or Project Manager experience
• WA mining construction experience
• Mineral processing plant or major industrial project experience
• Strong contractor management capability
• Demonstrated leadership of large multi-disciplinary workforces
• Sound commercial awareness
• Statutory mining experience including SSE, S26 or equivalent responsibilities highly regarded
• Ability to operate effectively within an owner's team environment

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to play a key role in the delivery of a high-profile WA resources project at a stage where strong site leadership will materially influence project outcomes.

Applications and confidential enquiries are welcomed from suitably qualified professionals currently available or becoming available in the near term.

For a confidential discussion contact Chris Platts on 0487 623 042

job.title: LATAM Credit Research Analyst
job.description:
LATAM Credit Research Analyst 

Company Overview
Our client is a leading global hedge fund with a robust systematic heritage and a rapidly expanding discretionary trading business. The firm has made significant investments in people, technology, and research capabilities to support its growth trajectory. Within the discretionary credit platform, the team is well resourced and strategically positioned to continue scaling throughout the year.

As part of this expansion, the fund is seeking an experienced LATAM Credit Research Analyst to join its discretionary credit group. This is a high-impact role offering the opportunity to work alongside a seasoned Portfolio Manager covering complex, event-driven opportunities across Latin America.

Role Overview
The Senior LATAM Credit Research Analyst will be responsible for delivering deep fundamental research across Latin American sovereign and quasi-sovereign issuers, with a particular focus on frontier and distressed emerging market situations. The role involves generating detailed, investment‑ready trade ideas and partnering closely with the Portfolio Manager to shape portfolio construction and risk positioning.
Coverage will include both local- and hard‑currency instruments, with exposure to cash bonds, derivatives (including CDS and warrants), and a range of special‑situation structures.
This role requires a hands‑on, highly analytical approach, strong familiarity with distressed and restructuring scenarios, and a willingness to travel extensively across the region to engage with policymakers, regulators, and senior leadership at state‑owned enterprises.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct deep-dive fundamental credit analysis on Latin American sovereign and quasi-sovereign issuers, including distressed and frontier markets (e.g., Argentina, Venezuela, Ecuador).
  • Develop, articulate, and maintain clear trade recommendations for implementation by the Portfolio Manager.
  • Evaluate complex capital structures and assess recovery values, restructuring outcomes, and downside scenarios.
  • Monitor macroeconomic, political, and idiosyncratic developments across assigned countries and issuers.
  • Build and maintain detailed financial models, valuation frameworks, and scenario analyses.
  • Formulate views across both cash and derivative instruments, including CDS and structured credit products.
  • Provide ongoing surveillance of existing positions, flagging material changes in creditworthiness or risk factors.
  • Collaborate closely with the Portfolio Manager and broader discretionary team to support portfolio strategy and risk management.
  • Travel frequently across Latin America to meet with government officials, central bank representatives, and senior executives of state-owned enterprises.
Required Qualifications
  • Approximately 10+ years of relevant experience in LATAM credit research, distressed EM investing, or sovereign/quasi-sovereign analysis.
  • Demonstrated track record in analysing frontier and distressed EM credit situations.
  • Expertise in evaluating restructuring scenarios, recovery analysis, and event-driven catalysts.
  • Strong understanding of both local and hard currency bonds, as well as derivatives (CDS, warrants, etc.).
  • Ability to synthesize complex political, macroeconomic, and credit data into actionable investment insights.
  • Exceptional financial modelling and analytical skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to produce crisp, decision‑ready research.
  • Willingness to travel extensively across Latin America.
  • Fluency in Spanish and/or Portuguese preferred but not required.
